title: Stratified surge fallback zones and proportional penalty credits
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket implements a new operational model for short-term surge capacity that reduces customer-visible overage shocks while preserving predictable fairness and abuse resistance. Key concepts are: (1) stratified fallback zones — ordered pools of compatible model/fleet variants used when primary dedicated capacity is saturated, and (2) proportional penalty credits — a reconciliation mechanism that refunds a calculated proportion of overage charges when temporary boosts are later covered by reserved capacity or credits.

Goals:
- Reduce invoices that show full overage charges for brief transient boosts when capacity is subsequently provisioned or absorbed.
- Provide operators per-fleet controls to carve out fallback zones (regional, GPU-class, quantized-model variants) and set priority fences for tenants.
- Ensure the system is deterministic and auditable for billing disputes.

Scope / Acceptance criteria:
1) Control-plane: new data model to register fallback zones per dedicated fleet. Each zone contains an ordered list of candidate capacity classes and a priority multiplier. Admin UI + API to modify zone definitions and fences.
2) Runtime: request routing policy aware of fallback zones that will prefer same-tenant capacity but can fall back under policy constraints (latency ceiling, model-compatibility tag).
3) Billing: track per-request metadata for fallback usage (zone id, fallback depth, timestamp) and implement proportional-penalty-credit algorithm that computes refund amount if capacity is later reclaimed or credits applied within a reconciliation window (configurable, default 7 days).
4) Operator controls: operator runbook + console controls to pause fallback routing for a fleet, drain fallback zones, and manually approve or cancel accumulated credits.
5) Telemetry: new metrics and traces: surge.fallback.count, surge.fallback.depth_histogram, surge.reconciliation.refund_amount, surge.reconciliation.window_violations, plus correlated logs to enable audits.
6) Backfill and reconciliation job to compute refunds and generate invoice adjustments; must be idempotent and support dry-run mode.

Technical design (high level):
- Fallback zone definition: small JSON blob stored in fleet metadata (fields: zone_id, ordered_candidates[], max_latency_ms, per_tenant_priority_map). Changes validated via API and versioned.
- Routing: extend smart-router to evaluate fallback zones when capacity shortfall detected for an incoming request. Evaluation uses: model compatibility score, latency penalty estimate, tenant priority factor, and operator-enforced fences. The router emits a fallback decision token that travels with the request into billing.
- Billing event model: augment existing per-request record with tags: "fallback_zone", "fallback_depth", "fallback_decision_ts", "fallback_override_reason". These are small strings.
- Proportional-penalty-credit algorithm (pseudocode):
  * When request R is served from fallback at time T, increment overage ledger for tenant with amount A (A = cost_at_served_rate). Mark entry as provisional with metadata (R_id, zone, depth).
  * Reconciliation window W starts at T. If within W a reserved capacity assignment or credit covers the provisional overage (e.g., tenant purchases commit or operator attributes capacity), compute refund = A * min(1, recovered_capacity_fraction * depth_weight). Depth_weight = 1 / (1 + fallback_depth). This reduces refund for deeper fallbacks.
  * Refunds are queued as line-item adjustments; if refund exceeds threshold X (configurable), require operator approval before applying to invoices.
- Fairness and anti-abuse: per-tenant surge rate limit; minimum dwell-time for provisional overage to be eligible for refund; anomaly detector to flag repeated short spikes.

Operational runbook (short):
- Detection: console alert when tentative refunds > $1k in 24h for a fleet.
- Investigate: open operator dashboard to view top tenants by provisional overage, fallback depth distribution, and correlated SLO/latency hits.
- Action: operators can 1) expand dedicated capacity, 2) adjust fallback zone ordering to prefer cheaper quantized variants, or 3) pause fallback routing for selected tenants.
- Reconciliation: run backfill job in dry-run for candidate window, review suggested refunds, then toggle apply mode.

Migration and rollout plan:
Phase 1 (canary): 2 fleets in staging+one small beta customer fleet. Enable only telemetry and routing decisions but do not create provisional overage charges. Duration 2 weeks.
Phase 2 (pilot billing): enable provisional overage ledger for 5 mid-size fleets; demonstrate end-to-end refund flow to internal finance team (dry-run and test invoices). Duration 4 weeks.
Phase 3 (gradual ramp): opt-in via console to enable proportional credits for selected customers; after 8 weeks, enable default for new dedicated customers.
Phase 4 (GA): enable automatic reconciliation and invoice adjustments with operator review thresholds.

APIs and Console changes:
- New Fleet API endpoints: POST /fleets/:id/fallback_zones, PUT /fleets/:id/fallback_zones/:zone_id, GET /fleets/:id/fallback_zones
- Console: Fallback Zones tab under Dedicated -> Fleets; operator toggles (pause routing, set fence, manual reconciliation).

Metrics and SLOs:
- Target: reduce % of customer invoices with >$250 unexpected overage within 24h from 6.4% to <2% for fleets with fallback enabled after three months.
- Latency SLOs: fallback decisions must be made within router decision budget (<=2ms added p95).
- Reconciliation accuracy: refunds computed must match audit trail in >99.9% of dry-run comparisons.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for router scoring and fallback depth computation.
- Integration tests for end-to-end tag propagation into billing and reconciliation job.
- Chaos tests: simulate rapid short spikes and verify idempotent reconciliation and no double refunds.
- Load test: ensure additional router decision overhead scales (target less than 5% CPU increase on router instances at 95th percentile).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: refunds could be gamed by tenants intentionally creating short spikes. Mitigation: minimum dwell-time and surge rate limit; require operator approval above thresholds; machine learning anomaly detector tuning.
- Risk: increased billing complexity causing confusion for customers. Mitigation: clear invoice line-item labels, console timeline for provisional entries, and customer-facing docs explaining proportional credit logic.
- Risk: operational burden on finance. Mitigation: start with dry-run and gradually enable auto-apply with conservative thresholds.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Default reconciliation window length (proposed 7 days, options 1/3/7/14).
- Threshold that requires operator approval (proposed $250).
- UI language for showing provisional vs applied charges.

Follow-ups and future work:
- Extend proportional credit formula to account for committed discounts and multi-day absorption patterns.
- Expose per-tenant provisional overage timeline in customer billing portal for self-service disputes.
- Research automated dispute resolution heuristics with finance and legal.
